summary: Drain recursively-enqueued process.nextTick callbacks before moving on to microtasks or later event-loop phases.

target.notes: Use the Node-compatible event-loop runtime; do not map ordering to arbitrary Task/ThreadPool scheduling.

semantics.drain_policy: next-tick queue is fully drained, including callbacks appended while draining
semantics.starvation: unbounded recursive nextTick scheduling can prevent I/O/timers from progressing
semantics.microtask_relation: microtasks run after the next-tick queue drain checkpoint

caveats: A naive one-item-per-turn scheduler changes ordering and avoids starvation that real Node code can observe.
Compiler/runtime may add diagnostics, but compatibility mode must preserve semantics.

tests.name: recursive chain can starve timer
tests.expected_behavior: the nextTick chain completes before the timer callback can run
